correctness.rationale: All 18 Hamming-pair isometry classes for 3<=n<=6 have complete face-level certificates. An independent Python 3 standard-library checker enumerated every clique (48,578 face occurrences), verified every free face has a unique maximal immediate coface, every critical face is maximal, all faces disappear, and only the displayed critical cells remain. The descending free-pair/critical-facet peeling produces an acyclic Forman matching; the resulting Morse CW model is one point plus only 2- or 3-dimensional cells, yielding the stated *integral homotopy* wedges. No extrapolation beyond dimension six.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2021 theorem for every initial binary segment gives all one-point removals and all distance-one two-point removals, which are expressly not claimed novel. It provides no general arbitrary-two-puncture theorem. The 2026 paper treats cohomology, connectivity and induced-subcomplex homology detection, not the homotopy census for two removed points. General line-graph topology identifies relevant links but not automatically the missing attaching maps for two-point deletions. All 12 cases with distance >=2 in n=4,5,6 were independently Morse-certified.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The two-puncture claim cannot be recovered merely by subtracting two one-vertex link Betti ranks: the map from the second link to the first punctured complex requires control of its attaching homotopy class. Theorem 8 yields distance one by cube symmetry, but not d>=2. The 2020 line-graph theorem covers the link graph and does not by itself determine the complement of two vertex stars. The 2026 paper does not give these attaching maps. The new exact perfect Morse matchings prove the entire spaces, not just Euler characteristics.

value.rationale: This is a complete, symmetry-reduced, reproducible integral homotopy census of deletion of two samples in binary Hamming cubes through six coordinates, rather than one arbitrary example or a Betti-number recalculation. It detects a sharp Hamming-distance-two/three transition in three consecutive nontrivial cube dimensions; the three-cube antipodal case also exhibits a dimension-two exception. Exact pair-deletion topology is motivated by robustness of Rips complexes to missing observations and is not determined by full-cube sphere counts. Finite all-orbit classification through the 64-point cube is a substantial explicit cutoff with 48,578 independently checked face occurrences; it is not presented as an all-dimensional law.
